the_defect_this_reading_found.summary: The probe in s3-10 called `the_walked_cell` was not the walked cell. It read the audit sheet's (286, 129) as an index into the PUBLISHED raster. Those numbers index the UTM GridSpec the pipeline computes on. The published raster is a WGS84 lon/lat grid with its own indexing and also has a cell (286, 129), about 400 m away, and the sheet's own lon/lat columns were unused. Codex pass 55 confirmed the cause by rebuilding the UTM grid: the sheet coordinate is the rounded centre of UTM cell (286, 129) and falls in published cell (282, 126).
the_defect_this_reading_found.why_it_mattered: The probe's own text called its card 'the one a person can check against a walk'. The two cells do not agree about anything a walker would check.
the_defect_this_reading_found.fixed: measure_drawn_pixel.py now derives the probe from the door's lon/lat and records which cell that is. Regenerating changed that one probe and nothing else: every other probe and every exposure figure is byte-identical.

the_costs_this_session_could_measure.card_round_trip_one_cell: 0.3 ms last / 0.2 ms median over 17 hovers
the_costs_this_session_could_measure.card_round_trip_note: the figure the card plan listed as unverified. It is a real browser message round trip on one desktop, measured between sending the request and receiving the reply: it does NOT include the DOM update, so it is not pointer-to-visible latency. CORRECTED 2026-11-16, Codex pass 55 F5: this said the figure 'matches the order of' the Node worker-side measurement and that one explainAt per pointer move is 'free'. 0.2 ms is 1,000 times 0.0002 ms, not the same order, and the handler figure excludes the message passing that dominates it. What it does support is retaining the current architecture on this desktop: no batching and no cached outcome plane are justified by anything measured here.
the_costs_this_session_could_measure.worker_compute_whole_raster: 7.7 ms last / 9.1 ms median over 20 scripted changes

the_cost_this_session_could_not_measure.what: slider to repaint, total -- the figure a household feels
the_cost_this_session_could_not_measure.what_the_page_reported: 1002.3 ms last / 1002.7 ms median over 20 changes
the_cost_this_session_could_not_measure.why_that_number_is_the_instrument: requestAnimationFrame was firing once a second. The page reported visibilityState 'visible', document.hidden false and hasFocus() true, because an OCCLUDED window is not a hidden document -- and Chrome throttles frames in a window nothing is displaying. Paint completion is detected on a frame, so every repaint measured one frame clock.
the_cost_this_session_could_not_measure.the_control: frame gaps sampled for ten seconds read 1000, 450, 33, 1000, 1000, 1000, 1000, 33, 17, 17, 17, 17, 17, 17, 17, 1000, 1017, 1000 ms. The run of 17 ms frames is exactly the window in which a screenshot was captured. CORRECTED 2026-11-16, Codex pass 55 F5: this concluded 'the page renders at 60 fps when something is looking at it'. The observation is a capture-associated burst of animation-frame callbacks; it does not establish product rendering performance, and it does not exclude the reading in which the one-second delay is real in that operating state and the capture is the intervention. BOTH readings are live. Foreground interactive latency is unresolved and needs a person with the window on screen.
the_cost_this_session_could_not_measure.the_one_sample_taken_after_a_capture: a single manual threshold change made immediately after two screen captures: 68.9 ms total, 54.8 ms transfer and paint, 13.5 ms compute. n=1, and reported as n=1. CORRECTED 2026-11-16, Codex pass 55 F5: this was called 'untainted'. It was taken immediately after the very intervention that is said to change frame scheduling, so it is evidence that a faster response occurred, not an unconfounded baseline.
the_cost_this_session_could_not_measure.to_measure_it_properly: click Auto-bench with the window actually on screen and read the stats row. One click, and it needs a person at the machine rather than a session.

run.what_zero_disagreements_would_mean: that the page places the raster exactly as measure_drawn_pixel.py predicts, including the sub-row displacement, so the structure counts in that artifact describe the page a household actually gets
run.what_this_cannot_see: an AFFINE placement error. The drawn row is recovered from where the quad's own corners project, so a constant offset or a uniform stretch of the texture cancels out and this probe reports agreement. Only the SHAPE of the placement is visible to it, which is the Mercator-against-latitude question it was built for. Closing the rest needs a rendered pixel: a screenshot at a colour edge, checked against the screen row predicted from corner_screen_y and drawn_rows_per_screen_pixel above.
